title: Saving a new description changes it at every location and on its core
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • You can switch to a second location, {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310), in the location switcher in the top bar.
  • Part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-DESCSAVE-01), with the description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL Desc Save) and a Core Charge (for example 15.00), is stocked at {Location-A} and {Location-B}.
  • {Part-A}'s core, {Core-A} (for example "Core for ZZAUTOTEST PL Desc Save"), comes from its Core Charge and has its own Part History page.
  • The new description is {Description-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL Desc Saved New).
custom_steps:
1. At {Location-A}, go to Parts → Inventory and type {Part-A} in the search.
  2. Click the {Part-A} row.
  3. Replace the Description with {Description-B}.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Go to Parts → Part Library and type {Part-A} in the search.
  6. Open the Part History page of {Core-A}.
  7. Pick {Location-B} in the location switcher.
  8. Go to Parts → Inventory and type {Part-A} in the search.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the window closes, and the {Location-A} row shows {Description-B}.
  • Step 5: the one entry shows Description {Description-B}.
  • Step 6: {Core-A}'s own Part History page names the core "Core for {Description-B}" and shows the entry "Description updated | Original description: Core for {Description-A} | New description: Core for {Description-B}". If no screen lets you open {Core-A}'s own Part History page, write "not checked by hand" for this step in the result comment.
  • Step 8: at {Location-B} the row also shows {Description-B}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S13-R14, S13-R15, S10-R24, S10-R26, S5-E3, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.3 (Saved: the list shows the new values), board 2.5 (Lethbridge: renamed there too), 13 Oct copy. Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S13-R14: “Saving a changed description changes the part's Part Library entry, so every location that stocks the part shows the new description.”
  • S13-R15: “A changed description also renames the part's core, which reads "Core for {description}".”
  • S10-R24: “A changed description writes "Description updated | Original description: {old} | New description: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.”
  • S10-R26: “When the part has a core, the core gets the same number or description entry. The core's description entries read its own description, "Core for {description}".”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
